250.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Gauri, Bavan Akhri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Gurdev is mother, the Gurdev is father, the Gurdev is the Master, the Supreme God. The Gurdev is the friend who destroys ignorance; the Gurdev is kinsman and brother born of the same womb. The Gurdev is the Giver who teaches the Lord's Name; the Gurdev's mantra is one whose power nothing can stop. The Gurdev is the embodiment of peace, truth and wisdom; the Gurdev is a paaras whose touch surpasses even the paaras. The Gurdev is the tirath, the pool of Amrit; to bathe in the Guru's wisdom is beyond all else. The Gurdev is the Creator, the remover of all sins; the Gurdev makes the fallen pure. The Gurdev is from the beginning, from the start of the ages, in every age; repeating the Gurdev's mantra, the Lord's Name, one is saved. O God, in your grace join (us) to the Gurdev's company, holding fast to which we foolish sinners may swim across. The Gurdev is the True Guru, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God; O Nanak, salutation to the Gurdev, the Lord. ॥1॥

Bavan Akhri (fifty-two letters): a composition in which each pauri opens with a letter of the alphabet (Ong, Sassa, Dhadha, Nganga and the rest); each salok gives the thought that the pauri after it unfolds.
250.2: (God) himself has done (all) and caused (all) to be done; he himself has the power to do (all). O Nanak, the One alone pervades all; there has been no other, and there will be none. ॥1॥
250.3: Ong: salutation to Oankar, to the Saadh, the True Guru, who in the beginning, in the middle and at the end is the Formless One. He himself is in Sunn; he himself is seated in bliss; he himself hears (his praise); he himself is the glorious One. He himself brought himself into being; he himself is (his own) father, he himself (his own) mother. He himself is the subtle (unseen), he himself the gross (the visible world). O Nanak, (his) play is beyond understanding. Show grace, O God, merciful to the meek, that (my) mind may become the dust of your Sants' feet.
Ong: the first letter of the alphabet, here also the name of Ik Oankar, the One God. Sunn (the void): the state before creation, when there was nothing but God.
250.4: The Formless One himself is (all) form; Nirgun and Sargun, he is the One. The One is spoken of as the One alone; O Nanak, the One is the many. ॥1॥
Nirgun: God beyond the three qualities of Maya; Sargun: God made manifest in the creation, with its qualities.
250.5: Ong: Oankar made the world of forms (for beings to become) Gurmukh; he is the One who strings (all) on a single thread. (He) has spread out the three qualities, each apart; from Nirgun (he) has come into sight as Sargun. (O God,) making every kind (of being, you) have brought forth (the world); (you) have made the mind's attachment, (the root of) birth and death, grow. (Yet you) yourself are apart from both (birth and death). O Nanak, (he) has no end, no near shore and no far shore. ॥2॥
250.6: They alone are bankers, they the wealthy, (who have) the wealth of truth, the capital of the Lord's (Name). O Nanak, truth and purity are found with such Sants. ॥1॥
250.7: Sassa: True, true, true is he; no one is apart from the True Being. He alone comes to (God's) refuge whom (God himself) brings there; remembering (him) again and again, he sings (his) praises and makes (others) hear them. Fear and doubt do not touch him at all; to him the glory of that (Lord) alone is plainly seen. He who reaches this (state) is the Saadh; Nanak is ever a sacrifice to him. ॥3॥
250.8: Why do (you) cry out, wealth, wealth? All attachment to Maya is false. O Nanak, without the Name all are turning to dust. ॥1॥
251.1: Dhadha: (O God,) the dust (of the feet) of your servants is pure; blessed are those whose mind longs for this (dust). (They) do not want wealth, nor do they wish for heaven; (they) are absorbed in the love of the most dear (Lord), and in the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh. How can worldly entanglements take hold of those who do not leave the One to go anywhere else? The one in whose heart God has placed (his) Name, O Nanak, that Saadh is the perfect Lord's own form. ॥4॥
251.2: By many religious garbs, by (talk of) knowledge and by meditation, by stubbornness of mind, no one has met (God). Says Nanak, the one on whom (God's) grace has come is the devotee, is the wise one. ॥1॥
251.3: Nganga: spiritual wisdom (does not come) by words of the mouth, nor by the many devices of the Shastras and their (many) ways. He alone is wise in whom that (Lord) is firmly fixed; by mere saying and hearing, no union (with God) comes about at all. He is wise in whom (God's) command stays firm; to him, heat and cold are all one. He is wise who, through the Guru, reflects on the essence, O Nanak, (the one) on whom (God) has bestowed his grace. ॥5॥
Nganga: for the acrostic, giaan (spiritual wisdom) and giaani (the wise) are spelt here with the letter ਙ.
251.4: Those who came into the world without understanding came in name only; they are beasts and cattle. O Nanak, he alone understands, through the Guru, on whose forehead (good) fortune is written. ॥1॥
251.5: (One) has come into this age for the One (Lord) alone, (yet) from birth Maya the enchantress has enchanted (him). In the hollow of the womb (beings) practise austerity upside down, (and there) they keep remembering God with every breath; (but once born) they are entangled in what they must leave behind, and they forget the Giver from their minds. O Master of the world, the one on whom (you) bestow grace says Nanak, does not forget (you) here or hereafter. ॥6॥
251.6: By (God's) Hukam (one) comes, by Hukam (one) perishes; no one is outside (his) command. Coming and going ends for him, O Nanak, in whose mind that (Lord dwells). ॥1॥
251.7: These beings dwell in many wombs; absorbed in sweet attachment, (they) are snared in births. This Maya has brought (them) under the three qualities; (she) has put her own attachment into every heart. O friend, tell (me) some remedy by which I may cross this hard (ocean of) Maya. (Whom God) in his grace joins to the Sat Sangat, O Nanak, Maya does not come near him. ॥7॥
251.8: The deeds that are done, good and bad, that God himself has done; (yet) the beast (of a man) cries, I, I, of himself; O Nanak, without the Lord what can (anyone) accomplish? ॥1॥
251.9: The One himself causes (all) to be done; he himself has spread out sin and virtue. In this age, to whatever (God) himself has attached (each one), that alone (each one) has received which he himself has caused to be given. No one knows his limit; whatever he does, that alone comes to pass. From the One alone comes the whole expanse; O Nanak, (he) himself is the One who sets (all) right. ॥8॥
251.10: (People) stay engrossed in the amusements of women; (yet) this clamour of poison (Maya) is (as fleeting as) the safflower's colour. Nanak seeks the refuge of that (Lord), through whom the sense of I and mine is destroyed. ॥1॥
252.1: O mind, wherever you lose yourself apart from the Lord, there, in each place, bonds are laid (on you). The Saakats practise the very ways by which there is no release anywhere. Those devoted to ritual deeds keep on saying I, I; the burden of that (ego) is beyond bearing. Without love for the Naam, these very deeds are vices. Through the pleasures of sweet Maya they are bound with the rope of Jam. Beguiled by delusion, they do not see that God stays with (them) always. When the account is reckoned, there is no release; a wall of unbaked clay does not become clean (by washing). O Nanak, the one to whom (God himself) gives understanding gains, through the Guru, a pure intellect. ॥9॥
252.2: The one whose bonds are broken has found the company of the Saadh. O Nanak, those who are dyed in the love of the One: deep (and fast) is their colour. ॥1॥
252.3: Rara: dye this mind of yours (in the Lord's love); repeat with your tongue the Name of the Lord, Har Har; keep up its repetition. (Then) in the Lord's court no one will call out to you with contempt; (rather, all) will greet you with honour: come, be seated. You will gain a dwelling in that mansion (of the Lord); (there) is no birth and death, nor any perishing. The one on whose forehead (the Lord's) grace is written from the very beginning: O Nanak, the wealth of the Lord (the Name) is in that one's home. ॥10॥
252.4: Greed, falsehood, vice and attachment hold sway over the blind fools; O Nanak, in the bonds of Maya they lie clinging to what is foul. ॥1॥
252.5: Lala: clinging to the pleasures of the senses, (people) are steeped in them; with an intellect full of ego, they are drunk on the wine of Maya. Caught in this Maya, they are born and die; as (God's) Hukam is, so do (beings) act. (Of oneself) no one is lacking and no one is complete; no one is wise and no one a fool. (O God,) to whatever you attach (them), to that they are attached. O Nanak, the Master is for ever untouched (by it all). ॥11॥
252.6: God is the Beloved, Gopal, Gobind; deep, profound and unfathomable is he. There is no other, none second (to him); O Nanak, he is the carefree Lord. ॥1॥
252.7: Lala: there is no one equal to him; he alone is, himself; there will be no other. Ever-existent, he has been for ever; no one has found his end. He fully pervades the worm and the elephant; the all-pervading Being is known to be manifest in every place. The one to whom the Lord has given his own sweet essence, O Nanak, repeats (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, through the Guru. ॥12॥
252.8: Those who have known the relish of the spirit savour the Lord's love in Sahaj; O Nanak, blessed, blessed, blessed are those people; their coming (into the world) is approved. ॥1॥
252.9: That one's coming (into the world) alone should be counted fruitful whose tongue utters the praise of the Lord, Har Har. Those who come and dwell in the Saadh's company meditate on the Naam night and day with love. That person, coming (into the world), stays dyed in the Naam on whom the Creator bestows kindness and mercy. He comes but once, and does not enter the cycle of births again; O Nanak, he is absorbed in the sight of the Lord. ॥13॥
252.10: The One by repeating whom bliss wells up in the mind and the love of another perishes, and pain, suffering and craving are quenched: O Nanak, merge in his Name. ॥1॥
253.1: Yaya: burn away evil-mindedness and duality; abandoning it, you will abide in peace and Sahaj. Yaya: go and seek the refuge of the Sants, with whose support this world-ocean is crossed. Yaya: that one does not come into birth (again) who takes the Name of the One and strings it into his mind. Yaya: with the support of the Perfect Guru, (this human) life is not lost; O Nanak, that one has found peace in whose heart is the One. ॥14॥
253.2: The Friend of this world and the next dwells within mind and body; the Perfect Guru has taught (this); O Nanak, one should repeat (his Name) every day. ॥1॥
253.3: Night and day remember him who will be your helper at the end. This Maya lasts but four or six days; everyone leaves it and goes. Whose are mother, father, son and daughter? Home, wife, anything at all: (no one) has taken it along. Gather such (wealth) as does not perish, (so that) you go with honour to your own home. Those who in Kalyug have sung (the Lord's) Kirtan in the Saadh Sangat: O Nanak, none of them has come (into birth) again. ॥15॥
253.4: (Though they be) very handsome, of noble birth, clever, eminent, learned and wealthy, O Nanak, those with no love for the Lord are called dead. ॥1॥
253.5: Nganga: (one may) be versed in the six Shastras, practise drawing in, holding and letting out the breath (purak, kumbhak, rechak), be given to knowledge and meditation, and bathe at places of pilgrimage, cook his own food (for purity), let no one touch him, and live in the wilderness; (but if) there is no love in his mind for the Name of the Lord, Ram, all that he has done is perishable. Higher than him I count the chandal in whose mind Gopal dwells, says Nanak. ॥16॥
Purak, kumbhak and rechak are the three parts of the yogis' breath control (pranayam). A sompaak cooks his own food for ritual purity; an aparas lets no one touch him.
253.6: (People) wander the four quarters and the ten directions by the line drawn by the deeds they have done; O Nanak, pleasure and pain, liberation and the cycle of births (come) by the writ that is written. ॥1॥
253.7: Kaka: he alone is the Creator, the maker of all causes; no one can erase the writ he has written. Nothing has to be done (by him) a second time; the Maker is not one who errs. To one he himself shows the path; another he makes to wander in the wilderness and repent. He himself has made his own play; O Nanak, whatever he has given, that is what (each) has received. ॥17॥
253.8: (His servants) go on eating, spending and enjoying, (yet his) storehouses are never used up. O Nanak, countless people repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har; there is no counting them. ॥1॥
253.9: Khakha: nothing is wanting with that almighty (Lord); whatever he is to give, he keeps giving, whatever place (one) may go to. The wealth of the Naam is their provision and their treasure; this is the devotees' capital. In forgiveness, humility, bliss and Sahaj, they keep repeating (the Name of) the Treasure of virtues. Those to whom (God) is merciful play and blossom in bliss; they are ever rich and graceful: the riches of the Lord's Name are in their home. No anguish, no pain, no penalty is theirs on whom he has cast his glance of grace. O Nanak, those who are pleasing to God have come through in full. ॥18॥
254.1: Count and measure, and see within your own mind: people must surely depart. Through the Guru, hope in passing things is erased; O Nanak, the Naam (alone) makes one whole. ॥1॥
254.2: Gaga: sing the virtues of Gobind; repeat (his Name) with every breath, every day. What trust can be placed in the body? Do not delay, my friend. Childhood, youth or old age: at none of these is there any bar (to death). No one knows the hour when the noose of Jam will come and fall. See: the learned, the meditative, the clever, (none) is to stay in this place. That which all the world has left behind and gone, to that the fools cling. By the Guru's grace, the one with (good) fortune on the forehead keeps remembering (the Lord). O Nanak, those granted the wedded love of the Beloved: their coming (into the world) bears fruit. ॥19॥
254.3: All the Shastras and Vedas have been searched through; none of them tells of any other (than him). In the beginning, from the start of the ages, now and in time to come, O Nanak, he alone is. ॥1॥
254.4: Ghagha: set this firmly in your mind: apart from the Lord there is no other. There has been none, nor will there be; everywhere he alone is contained. O mind, you will melt into (him) only when you come to (his) refuge. In Kalyug the Naam is the essence, (and it is the true) act of atonement. Many toil and toil (at other efforts), and repent; without devotion to the Lord, where can they find steadiness? That one has mixed and drunk the supremely sweet Amrit, O Nanak, (that one) to whom the Guru has given the Lord's (Name). ॥20॥
Punahcharan: a rite of expiation, performed to wipe out the effect of a sin.
254.5: (God) has sent (each one into the world) with all the days and breaths counted; they do not grow or shrink by even a sesame seed's worth. Those who, in delusion and attachment, long to live (longer), O Nanak, are fools. ॥1॥
254.6: Nganga: death seizes those whom God has made Saakats; they are born and die in countless forms of life, (for) they have not recognised the Lord within (Atam Ram). Divine knowledge and meditation come only to those on whom (God) himself, in his grace, has had them bestowed. By counting and reckoning (deeds) no one is set free; the pitcher of unbaked clay will surely break. He alone (truly) lives who, while alive, has repeated (the Name); O Nanak, (such ones) become manifest; they do not stay hidden. ॥21॥
254.7: I fix my mind on (the Lord's) lotus feet, and the inverted lotus (of the heart) blossoms. O Nanak, through the counsel of the Sants, Gobind himself becomes manifest (in the heart). ॥1॥
In ਗੋੁਬਿੰਦ the letter ਗ carries two vowel signs (ੋ and ੁ); it is read gubind, to keep the metre of the line.
254.8: Chacha: (when I) was joined to the Guru's lotus feet, blessed, blessed was that day, and fortunate that union. (Before,) I had wandered through the four quarters and the ten directions; when (the Lord's) grace came, then I was granted the sight (of him). My thoughts were made fair, and all duality perished; in the Saadh Sangat the mind became pure. He puts away all worry and beholds the One (everywhere), O Nanak, the one whose eyes bear the collyrium of (the Guru's) wisdom. ॥22॥
254.9: Singing songs of Gobind's virtues, the heart grows cool and the mind is at ease. Show such grace, O God; Nanak is the servant of your servants. ॥1॥
254.10: Chhachha: (O God,) we are your little servants, carriers of water for the servants of your servants. Chhachha: (grant that we) become the dust (of the feet) of your Sants; show your grace, O Lord. (One who,) giving up cleverness and much cunning, has set the support of the Sants firm in the mind: even (that) puppet of dust has attained the supreme state, O Nanak, the one whom the Sants help. ॥23॥
255.1: (People) swell with pride through force and oppression; (their) frail body (is given over) to vice. Through the proud intellect they are caught in bonds; O Nanak, release (comes only) through the Name. ॥1॥
255.2: Jaja: one who thinks, I have become someone, is held fast in that delusion, like a parrot on the nalini. When one thinks, I am a devotee, a man of wisdom, hereafter the Master will not count it worth a sesame seed. When one thinks, I am a preacher (of holy discourse), he goes about the earth like a pedlar. The one who has slain Haumai in the Saadh Sangat, O Nanak, meets Murari, the Lord. ॥24॥

The nalini is a parrot trap: a reed that turns on a rod set over a bowl of water, with grain on it. When the parrot perches, the reed turns over; seeing the water below, the frightened bird clings to it and so is caught by its own hold.
255.3: Rise in the early hours and repeat the Naam; worship (the Lord) night and day. No fretting will take hold of you; says Nanak, (your) troubles will end. ॥1॥
255.4: Jhajha: your fretting will end: trade in the Name of Ram. Fretting and fretting, the Saakat dies, the one in whose heart is the love of another. The stains and sins of your mind will fall away (if) you hear (the Lord's) nectar-like praise in the company of the Sants. Lust, anger and wickedness fall away (from that one), O Nanak, on whom is the grace of the Lord of the world. ॥25॥
255.5: You may try in many ways, friend, (but) you will not be allowed to stay (here). Says Nanak: if you worship the Lord, Har Har, with love for the Name, you will (truly) live. ॥1॥
255.6: Nyanya: know this firmly as certain, that these attachments perish. How many have risen and gone (from here) I do not reckon, nor can I count them. Whatever I see is passing away; with whom, then, should one keep company? O mind, know it truly in this way: the colour of Maya is false. That one alone knows it, that one is a Sant, who has been set apart from delusion. (O God,) the one with whom you are well pleased you draw out of the blind well (of attachment). The One in whose hands is all power, who is able to bring every cause about, Nanak sings the praise of him who has brought about (this) union. ॥26॥
255.7: The bonds of birth and death are broken, and peace is found, by serving the Saadh, O Nanak, (by one) from whose mind Gobind the King, the treasure of virtues, is never forgotten. ॥1॥
255.8: If you would serve, serve the One, from whom no one (goes away) empty. (When he) dwells in mind, body, mouth and heart, whatever you wish comes to be. Service in (the Lord's) mansion is given to the one on whom the Saadh is kind; and one comes to dwell in the Saadh Sangat only when (the Lord) himself is merciful. I have searched through many places; without the Name there is no peace. The messengers of Jam turn away from those who merge into the company of the Saadh. Again and again I am a sacrifice to the Sants; O Nanak, (in their company) the sins of ages long past have been destroyed. ॥27॥
255.9: (O God,) no bar is put in the way at (your) door of those with whom you are well pleased. Blessed, blessed indeed, O Nanak, are those whom God has made his own. ॥1॥
256.1: Thattha: they do not wound (anyone's) heart who leave all else behind and cling to the One alone. Those who have died clashing and jostling (with others) for the sake of Maya have known well-being nowhere. Coolness came upon the one who dwelt in the company of the Sants; there the nectar of the Name filled (that one's) soul with its taste. The one who has become pleasing to his Master, O Nanak, that one's mind has been cooled and calmed. ॥28॥
256.2: Countless times I bow and lie prostrate (before you), O mighty (Lord) of every power. Keep Nanak from wavering, O God: give him your hand. ॥1॥
256.3: Dadda: this is not (your lasting) dwelling; come to know where the dwelling is. Through the Guru's Shabad, learn the way to that dwelling. For this dwelling one toils and labours, yet not a jot of it goes along (at the end). The ways of that dwelling are known to that one on whom rests the glance (of grace) of the perfect Lord. (Those who) have found the unmoving, true dwelling in the Saadh Sangat — O Nanak, those people do not waver. ॥29॥
256.4: When Dharam Raj (and his messengers) began to tear down (the body), no one put up a barrier (before them). O Nanak, those bound in kinship with the Saadh Sangat were saved by repeating (the Name of) the Lord. ॥1॥
256.5: Dhaddha: where do you go searching? The search is within this mind. God dwells with you; why do you roam from forest to forest? In the Saadh Sangat, pull down the mound of the dreadful proud intellect; (then) you will find peace, dwell in Sahaj, and be filled with joy beholding (the Lord). (While) the mound (of ego) stands, one is born only to die, and suffers the pains of the womb and of births; drunk with attachment, one stays clinging (to Maya), and, crying I, I, keeps coming and going. Crumbling, crumbling, (we) have now fallen at the refuge of the holy; the nooses of pain have been cut, and, O Nanak, (the Lord) has merged (us into himself). ॥30॥
256.6: (Dharam Raj says:) Where the Saadhs worship Gobind and sing his Kirtan day by day, O Nanak, (go there, and) neither I nor you will escape: do not go near it, my messengers. ॥1॥
256.7: Nanna: on the battlefield (of life), the one who conquers the self wins. One who fights Haumai and duality and dies (to the self) becomes a glorious warrior. One who, by the teaching of the perfect Guru, wipes out the ego and dies while yet alive, conquers the mind and meets the Lord: his is the garb of the warrior. He counts no one as his own; the One alone is his shelter and stay. Night and day he keeps remembering God, the boundless Being. He makes this mind the dust (of the feet) of all; such are the deeds he lives by. He understands (the Lord's) Hukam and (knows) lasting peace; O Nanak, he receives what was written (for him). ॥31॥
256.8: I would offer body, mind and wealth to the one who would unite me with God. O Nanak, (meeting him,) doubt and fear are cut away, and the watching eye of Jam is gone. ॥1॥
256.9: Tata: love him, Gobind the King, the treasure of virtues; you will obtain the fruits your mind longs for, and your burning will leave you. Dread of the road of Jam is gone for the one in whose mind the Name dwells. You will reach the high state, your understanding will be lit, and you will find a place in (the Lord's) mansion. Wealth does not go along with (anyone at the end), nor house, nor youth, nor power. In the company of the Sants keep remembering (the Lord); this alone will serve you. No burning grief remains at all when (the Lord) himself takes the fever away. O Nanak, (the Lord) cherishes us; he himself is mother and father. ॥32॥
257.1: (They) have grown weary toiling in many ways, yet are not satisfied, and (their) craving has not left them. Amassing and amassing (Maya), the Saakats have died; O Nanak, Maya did not go with them. ॥1॥
257.2: Thatha: no one stays (here) for ever; why, then, do you stretch out your feet (as if to stay)? You practise countless frauds, tricks and deceits, striving for Maya alone. You fill your purse, you toil, and you drop exhausted, you fool; (yet) it is of no use to the soul at the last hour. You will find steadiness if you worship Gobind and take the teaching of the Sants; love the One for ever: this is the true love. (The Lord is) the cause, the doer and the one who has all things done; every means is in the hands of the One alone. Says Nanak: wherever you set them, (O Lord,) there they are set; the creatures are helpless. ॥33॥
257.3: (The Lord's) servants have seen the One as the giver of everything; with every breath they keep remembering (him); O Nanak, beholding (him) is what sustains them. ॥1॥
257.4: Dada: the Giver is the One, who gives to all; his giving never runs short; numberless are (his) brimming storehouses. The Giver lives for ever; O foolish mind, why have you forgotten him? My friend, the fault lies with no one; God (himself) has made the bond of attachment to Maya. Those whose pain you yourself take away, (O Lord,) O Nanak, each of them is fulfilled, through the Guru. ॥34॥
257.5: O my soul, take the One as your sole support, and put away hope in others; O Nanak, the Naam should be meditated on; (then) every task turns out well. ॥1॥
257.6: Dhadha: the wandering (of the mind) ends only when one's dwelling is in the company of the Sants. (O Lord,) when you yourself show grace from the very source, then light dawns in the mind. They whose wealth is lasting are the true merchants, whose capital is the Lord, Har Har, and who have traded in the Name. Steadfastness, praise and honour become the lot of the one who has heard the Name of the Lord, Har Har, with (his) ears. The one in whose heart (the Lord) stays absorbed, through the Guru: O Nanak, that servant (of the Lord) has received greatness. ॥35॥
257.7: O Nanak, (those who) have repeated the Naam, the Naam alone, with love, within and without, have been taught by the Perfect Guru; in the Saadh Sangat there is no hell (for them). ॥1॥
257.8: Nana: they do not fall into hell in whose mind and body the Naam dwells. Those who, through the Guru, repeat the Naam, the treasure, do not waste away in the poison of Maya. They meet with no refusal (anywhere), those to whom the Guru has given the mantra of the Naam. They are full of the Lord's Amrit, the treasure of treasures; there (within them), O Nanak, the unstruck instruments play. ॥36॥
258.1: The Guru, the Supreme Lord, has kept the honour (of the one) who has given up deceit, attachment and vice; O Nanak, let us worship that One alone, who has no end and no shore on either side. ॥1॥
258.2: Pappa: (the Lord) is beyond measure; (no one) has found his limit. The Lord King is beyond reach, the purifier of the fallen. Millions of wrongdoers become pure who meet the Saadh and repeat the Naam, the Amrit. Deceit, treachery and attachment are erased through (your) praise in the one whom you yourself protect, O Master of the world. He alone is the Emperor, with the canopy over (his) head; O Nanak, there is no other, no second (like him). ॥37॥
258.3: The nooses are cut, the wanderings are over; victory has come by conquering the mind. O Nanak, steadiness was found from the Guru, and the rounds (of birth) are over for ever. ॥1॥
258.4: Phapha: wandering and wandering (through births), you have come; (now) in Kalyug you have obtained the (human) body, so rarely given. Such a chance will not come to hand again. Repeat the Naam, and the nooses (of Maya) will be cut; there will be no coming and going again and again. Repeat the remembrance of that One, the One alone. Be merciful, O God, the Creator, and unite helpless Nanak with yourself. ॥38॥
258.5: Hear (my) prayer, O Supreme Lord, Gopal, merciful to the meek: for Nanak, the dust of the Saadhs' feet is comfort, wealth, many pleasures and delights. ॥1॥
258.6: Babba: those who know Brahm (God) are the (true) Brahmins; (true) Vaishnavs are they who, through the Guru, (keep) the dharma of purity. The hero is one who wipes out the evil in himself; no evil comes near him. (Man) is bound by his own bond of I, I (Haumai), (yet) the blind one puts the blame on others. All talk and cleverness come to nothing; only the one to whom you, (O Lord,) give understanding knows (this), says Nanak. ॥39॥
258.7: In your mind worship the Lord, the breaker of fear, the destroyer of sin and sorrow. Those in whose heart (the Lord) has come to dwell through the company of the Sants, O Nanak, do not wander in delusion. ॥1॥
258.8: Bhabha: wipe out your delusion; this whole world is a dream. Heavenly beings, men, goddesses and gods have wandered in delusion; Siddhas, seekers and (the likes of) Brahma have wandered in delusion. Wandering on and on in delusion, people have been led astray. This Maya is hard to cross, and most perilous. Those who, through the Guru, have wiped out delusion, fear and attachment, O Nanak, have found the supreme peace. ॥40॥
258.9: Maya wavers in many ways, (yet) the mind clings to it; (O Lord,) the one you keep from begging (for Maya) is in love with the Name alone, says Nanak. ॥1॥
258.10: Mamma: the one who begs is ignorant; the all-knowing Giver goes on giving. What he gave, he gave once (for all). O foolish mind, why do you keep crying out? Whenever you ask, you ask for things other (than the Name), through which no one has ever fared well. If you must ask, then ask for the One alone, by whom, says Nanak, you will cross to the far shore. ॥41॥
259.1: Their understanding is complete, and they are foremost, whose minds hold the teaching of the Perfect Guru; those who have come to know their God, O Nanak, are blessed with good fortune. ॥1॥
259.2: Mamma: one who has recognised (the Lord's) secret is content (in mind) as soon as he meets the Saadh Sangat. Pain and pleasure are weighed alike in his mind; he is spared from being born into hell or heaven. (He sees that) the same (Lord) is with (all), and the same (Lord) is untouched (by all); the Being fills each and every heart, (and he) sees (this) distinctly. In that relish (of the Lord) he alone has found peace; O Nanak, Maya does not stain him. ॥42॥
259.3: Listen, friends, companions, dear ones: without the Lord there is no release. O Nanak, their bonds are cut who fall at the Guru's feet. ॥1॥
259.4: Yaya: (people) make efforts of many kinds, (but) how far can success go without the one Name? The effort by which release comes is the company of the Saadh. Everyone holds (in mind) this longing to be saved, (but) without meditating on him there is no saving. He alone is the boat that carries across, mighty to save; save (us), the virtueless, O Lord of men. Those to whom (the Lord) himself has given this understanding in mind, word and deed, O Nanak, their understanding has come to light. ॥43॥
259.5: Hold no grudge against anyone; reflect on your own self. Live humbly in the world; O Nanak, by (the Lord's) gracious glance you will cross over. ॥1॥
259.6: Rara: (become the dust of the Lord,) whose dust all (creation) becomes; give up pride, and the arrears (in the account of your deeds) will be cleared. O brother, you will win through on the battlefield (of the world) and in the Lord's court when, through the Guru, you are lovingly attuned to the Name of Ram. Little by little the vices fall away, countless as they are, through the Shabad of the Perfect Guru. Dyed in love, they are intoxicated with the relish of the Name, those on whom, O Nanak, the Lord, the Guru, has bestowed this gift. ॥44॥
259.7: Greed, falsehood, vice and disease dwell in this body; one who has drunk the Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, through the Guru, O Nanak, dwells in peace. ॥1॥
259.8: Lala: anyone to whom I apply the medicine (of the Name), his pains and sorrows vanish in an instant. One who holds the medicine of the Name dear in the heart is not touched by disease even in a dream. The Lord's medicine is in all hearts, O brother, (but) without the Perfect Guru, the way (to take it) is not found. The Perfect Guru has set the regimen (to keep with it); then, O Nanak, pain does not come again. ॥45॥
259.9: Vasudev (the Lord) fills every place; in no place is he wanting. He is with (all), within and without; O Nanak, how can anything be hidden (from him)? ॥1॥
Vasudev: a name of Krishna, son of Vasudeva; in Gurbani it names God, who dwells in all.
259.10: Vava: bear enmity toward no one; Brahm (God) dwells within each and every heart. Vasudev pervades water and land; (but) only a rare one, by the Guru's grace, has reached (him). Enmity and opposition are gone from the minds of those who, through the Guru, listen to the Lord's Kirtan. Above all castes and marks stands the one who, O Nanak, utters Har Har through the Guru. ॥46॥
260.1: Crying I, I, the foolish, ignorant Saakats have passed (their lives); writhing, they died like the thirsty; O Nanak, (it was) by the deeds they had earned. ॥1॥
260.2: Rarra: the rankling strife (of the mind) ends in the company of the Saadh; worship of the Name is the essence of (all) rites and religious duties. The one in whose heart the Beautiful (Lord) has come to dwell: his strife is ended and destroyed. The foolish Saakats keep up strife, in whose hearts are the vices of the proud intellect. Rarra: the one who through the Guru has wiped out the strife is given understanding in an instant, O Nanak. ॥47॥
260.3: O mind, take hold of the Saadh's support; give up argument and cleverness. O Nanak, the one in whose mind the Guru's teaching dwells has good fortune (written) on the forehead. ॥1॥
260.4: Sassa: (O God,) defeated, we have now fallen at (your) refuge. The Shastras, the Smritis and the Vedas cry it aloud, and searching and searching, (we too) have searched and reflected: without worship of the Lord there is no release. With every breath we go astray; you are all-powerful, beyond count, boundless. O Merciful One, keep (the honour) of the one who has fallen at your refuge. Says Nanak, we are your children, O Gopal. ॥48॥
260.5: When self-conceit was gone, then peace came, and mind and body were made whole. O Nanak, (then) the One worthy of praise came into sight. ॥1॥
260.6: Khakha: I praise him with all my heart, who in an instant fills the empty to the brim. When the mortal becomes truly humble, (he) meditates night and day on God, who is free of all desire. If it pleases the Master, he gives that one peace. Such is the Supreme Lord, beyond all count: (he) forgives countless sins in an instant. O Nanak, the Master is merciful for ever. ॥49॥
260.7: I tell you the truth, listen, O my mind: fall at the refuge of the Lord King. O Nanak, when (one) gives up all argument and cleverness, (the Lord) takes (that one) into himself. ॥1॥
260.8: Sassa: give up cleverness, you ignorant one; God is not won over by cunning or by commanding. You may practise cleverness in a thousand ways, (yet) not one of them goes with you. Repeat him, him alone, day and night; O soul, (he alone) goes with you as your companion. The one whom (God) himself sets to serve the Saadh, O Nanak, no suffering touches him. ॥50॥
260.9: Speak Har, Har with the mouth; (when the Lord) dwells in the mind, peace comes. O Nanak, he pervades all; he is in every place and in the spaces between. ॥1॥
260.10: I look, and see the Lord filling every heart of all. Ever and for ever (the Lord) has been the destroyer of suffering: (this is) the Guru's wisdom. When Haumai is shed, bliss comes to that one; where there is no Haumai, there (God) himself is. Through the power of the company of the Sants, the sufferings of birth and death are destroyed. The one who lovingly holds firm (in the heart) the Name of the Merciful (Lord), in the company of the Sants, (God) becomes kind (to him). No one has done anything apart from him; O Nanak, all has come from God. ॥51॥
261.1: If (our deeds) are reckoned, there is no release anywhere; moment by moment we go astray. O Forgiver, forgive (us), and carry Nanak across. ॥1॥
261.2: (The mortal) is untrue to his salt, a sinner, a stranger (to God), of little understanding; he does not know the One, the very essence, who gave him soul, body and comforts. For the gain of Maya he goes searching in the ten directions, (but) not for an instant does he keep in mind God, the bountiful Giver. Greed, falsehood, vice and attachment: this is the wealth (he holds) in his mind. With lechers, thieves and great slanderers his (life) goes by. (O God,) if it pleases you, you forgive the false together with the true. O Nanak, if it pleases the Supreme Lord, stones float on water. ॥52॥
261.3: Eating, drinking, playing and laughing, (we) have wandered through many births. Lift (us) out of the world-ocean, God; Nanak leans on you (alone). ॥1॥
261.4: Playing and playing, (the soul) has come through many births, suffering pain. Meeting the Saadh, merging in the True Guru's word, (its) troubles are ended. (It) took up forgiveness, gathered truth, and ate the Amrit of the Naam; the Master's great grace came, (and it found) bliss, peace and rest. (It) carried its trading through, made great profit, and came home with honour; the Guru gave (it) true comfort, and the Lord came and met (it). (The Lord) himself has done (all), and he himself does it; he himself is ahead and behind. O Nanak, let us praise him alone, who pervades every heart. ॥53॥
261.5: O God, treasure of mercy, merciful One, (we) have come to (your) refuge. O Nanak, (when) the One, the imperishable Lord, dwells in the mind, (one) is filled with joy. ॥1॥
261.6: God has set the three worlds within letters; with letters, written again and again, the Vedas were pondered. In letters are the Shastras, the Smritis and the Puranas; in letters, sacred sound, speech and exposition. In letters (are told) fear and doubt and the way of release (from them); in letters, rites, deeds, purity and dharma. All that is seen is within letters; (but) O Nanak, the Supreme Lord is untouched (by them). ॥54॥

Akhar: in this pauri, letters, the written and spoken word in which the whole visible world is named and known; in the salok before it, akhar (Sanskrit akshara, the imperishable) is the imperishable Lord, who is untouched by letters.
261.7: The pen is in the hand of the Inaccessible; (he) writes (the destiny) on (every) forehead. He of incomparable beauty is entwined with all. (O God,) your praise cannot be told by the mouth. Beholding your sight, Nanak is enraptured, and is a sacrifice (to you). ॥1॥
261.8: O Unshakeable One, O Supreme Lord, Imperishable, Destroyer of sins, O Perfect One, O All-pervading, Destroyer of suffering, Treasure of virtues, O Companion, O Formless, O Nirgun, Support of all, O Gobind, O Treasury of virtues, in whom discernment ever abides, O Lord beyond the beyond, Har Hare: you are, and you will be. O ever-present with the Sants, Support of those who have none: O Master, I am your lowly servant; I am without virtue, I have no virtue at all. Grant Nanak the gift of the Naam, that I may keep it strung in my heart. ॥55॥
262.1: The Gurdev is mother, the Gurdev is father, the Gurdev is the Master, the Supreme God. The Gurdev is the friend who destroys ignorance; the Gurdev is kinsman and brother born of the same womb. The Gurdev is the Giver who teaches the Lord's Name; the Gurdev's mantra is one whose power nothing can stop. The Gurdev is the embodiment of peace, truth and wisdom; the Gurdev is a paaras whose touch surpasses even the paaras. The Gurdev is the tirath, the pool of Amrit; to bathe in the Guru's wisdom is beyond all else. The Gurdev is the Creator, the remover of all sins; the Gurdev makes the fallen pure. The Gurdev is from the beginning, from the start of the ages, in every age; repeating the Gurdev's mantra, the Lord's Name, one is saved. O God, in your grace join (us) to the Gurdev's company, holding fast to which we foolish sinners may swim across. The Gurdev is the True Guru, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God; O Nanak, salutation to the Gurdev, the Lord. This salok is to be read at the beginning and at the end (of the Bavan Akhri).

250.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Gauri, Bavan Akhri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Gurdev is mother, the Gurdev is father, the Gurdev is the Master, the Supreme God.
The Gurdev is the friend who destroys ignorance; the Gurdev is kinsman and brother born of the same womb.
The Gurdev is the Giver who teaches the Lord's Name; the Gurdev's mantra is one whose power nothing can stop.
The Gurdev is the embodiment of peace, truth and wisdom; the Gurdev is a paaras whose touch surpasses even the paaras.
The Gurdev is the tirath, the pool of Amrit; to bathe in the Guru's wisdom is beyond all else.
The Gurdev is the Creator, the remover of all sins; the Gurdev makes the fallen pure.
The Gurdev is from the beginning, from the start of the ages, in every age; repeating the Gurdev's mantra, the Lord's Name, one is saved.
O God, in your grace join (us) to the Gurdev's company, holding fast to which we foolish sinners may swim across.
The Gurdev is the True Guru, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God; O Nanak, salutation to the Gurdev, the Lord. ॥1॥
250.2: (God) himself has done (all) and caused (all) to be done; he himself has the power to do (all).
O Nanak, the One alone pervades all; there has been no other, and there will be none. ॥1॥
250.3: Ong: salutation to Oankar, to the Saadh, the True Guru,
who in the beginning, in the middle and at the end is the Formless One.
He himself is in Sunn; he himself is seated in bliss;
he himself hears (his praise); he himself is the glorious One.
He himself brought himself into being;
he himself is (his own) father, he himself (his own) mother.
He himself is the subtle (unseen), he himself the gross (the visible world).
O Nanak, (his) play is beyond understanding.
Show grace, O God, merciful to the meek,
that (my) mind may become the dust of your Sants' feet.
250.4: The Formless One himself is (all) form; Nirgun and Sargun, he is the One.
The One is spoken of as the One alone; O Nanak, the One is the many. ॥1॥
250.5: Ong: Oankar made the world of forms (for beings to become) Gurmukh;
he is the One who strings (all) on a single thread.
(He) has spread out the three qualities, each apart;
from Nirgun (he) has come into sight as Sargun.
(O God,) making every kind (of being, you) have brought forth (the world);
(you) have made the mind's attachment, (the root of) birth and death, grow.
(Yet you) yourself are apart from both (birth and death).
O Nanak, (he) has no end, no near shore and no far shore. ॥2॥
250.6: They alone are bankers, they the wealthy, (who have) the wealth of truth, the capital of the Lord's (Name).
O Nanak, truth and purity are found with such Sants. ॥1॥
250.7: Sassa: True, true, true is he;
no one is apart from the True Being.
He alone comes to (God's) refuge whom (God himself) brings there;
remembering (him) again and again, he sings (his) praises and makes (others) hear them.
Fear and doubt do not touch him at all;
to him the glory of that (Lord) alone is plainly seen.
He who reaches this (state) is the Saadh;
Nanak is ever a sacrifice to him. ॥3॥
250.8: Why do (you) cry out, wealth, wealth? All attachment to Maya is false.
O Nanak, without the Name all are turning to dust. ॥1॥
251.1: Dhadha: (O God,) the dust (of the feet) of your servants is pure;
blessed are those whose mind longs for this (dust).
(They) do not want wealth, nor do they wish for heaven;
(they) are absorbed in the love of the most dear (Lord), and in the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh.
How can worldly entanglements take hold of those
who do not leave the One to go anywhere else?
The one in whose heart God has placed (his) Name,
O Nanak, that Saadh is the perfect Lord's own form. ॥4॥
251.2: By many religious garbs, by (talk of) knowledge and by meditation, by stubbornness of mind, no one has met (God).
Says Nanak, the one on whom (God's) grace has come is the devotee, is the wise one. ॥1॥
251.3: Nganga: spiritual wisdom (does not come) by words of the mouth,
nor by the many devices of the Shastras and their (many) ways.
He alone is wise in whom that (Lord) is firmly fixed;
by mere saying and hearing, no union (with God) comes about at all.
He is wise in whom (God's) command stays firm;
to him, heat and cold are all one.
He is wise who, through the Guru, reflects on the essence,
O Nanak, (the one) on whom (God) has bestowed his grace. ॥5॥
251.4: Those who came into the world without understanding came in name only; they are beasts and cattle.
O Nanak, he alone understands, through the Guru, on whose forehead (good) fortune is written. ॥1॥
251.5: (One) has come into this age for the One (Lord) alone,
(yet) from birth Maya the enchantress has enchanted (him).
In the hollow of the womb (beings) practise austerity upside down,
(and there) they keep remembering God with every breath;
(but once born) they are entangled in what they must leave behind,
and they forget the Giver from their minds.
O Master of the world, the one on whom (you) bestow grace
says Nanak, does not forget (you) here or hereafter. ॥6॥
251.6: By (God's) Hukam (one) comes, by Hukam (one) perishes; no one is outside (his) command.
Coming and going ends for him, O Nanak, in whose mind that (Lord dwells). ॥1॥
251.7: These beings dwell in many wombs;
absorbed in sweet attachment, (they) are snared in births.
This Maya has brought (them) under the three qualities;
(she) has put her own attachment into every heart.
by which I may cross this hard (ocean of) Maya.
(Whom God) in his grace joins to the Sat Sangat,
O Nanak, Maya does not come near him. ॥7॥
251.8: The deeds that are done, good and bad, that God himself has done;
(yet) the beast (of a man) cries, I, I, of himself; O Nanak, without the Lord what can (anyone) accomplish? ॥1॥
251.9: The One himself causes (all) to be done;
he himself has spread out sin and virtue.
In this age, to whatever (God) himself has attached (each one),
that alone (each one) has received which he himself has caused to be given.
whatever he does, that alone comes to pass.
From the One alone comes the whole expanse;
O Nanak, (he) himself is the One who sets (all) right. ॥8॥
251.10: (People) stay engrossed in the amusements of women; (yet) this clamour of poison (Maya) is (as fleeting as) the safflower's colour.
Nanak seeks the refuge of that (Lord), through whom the sense of I and mine is destroyed. ॥1॥
252.1: O mind, wherever you lose yourself apart from the Lord, there, in each place, bonds are laid (on you).
The Saakats practise the very ways by which there is no release anywhere.
Those devoted to ritual deeds keep on saying I, I; the burden of that (ego) is beyond bearing.
Without love for the Naam, these very deeds are vices.
Through the pleasures of sweet Maya they are bound with the rope of Jam.
Beguiled by delusion, they do not see that God stays with (them) always.
When the account is reckoned, there is no release; a wall of unbaked clay does not become clean (by washing).
O Nanak, the one to whom (God himself) gives understanding gains, through the Guru, a pure intellect. ॥9॥
252.2: The one whose bonds are broken has found the company of the Saadh.
O Nanak, those who are dyed in the love of the One: deep (and fast) is their colour. ॥1॥
252.3: Rara: dye this mind of yours (in the Lord's love);
repeat with your tongue the Name of the Lord, Har Har; keep up its repetition.
(Then) in the Lord's court no one will call out to you with contempt;
(rather, all) will greet you with honour: come, be seated.
You will gain a dwelling in that mansion (of the Lord);
(there) is no birth and death, nor any perishing.
The one on whose forehead (the Lord's) grace is written from the very beginning:
O Nanak, the wealth of the Lord (the Name) is in that one's home. ॥10॥
252.4: Greed, falsehood, vice and attachment hold sway over the blind fools;
O Nanak, in the bonds of Maya they lie clinging to what is foul. ॥1॥
252.5: Lala: clinging to the pleasures of the senses, (people) are steeped in them;
with an intellect full of ego, they are drunk on the wine of Maya.
Caught in this Maya, they are born and die;
as (God's) Hukam is, so do (beings) act.
(Of oneself) no one is lacking and no one is complete;
no one is wise and no one a fool.
(O God,) to whatever you attach (them), to that they are attached.
O Nanak, the Master is for ever untouched (by it all). ॥11॥
252.6: God is the Beloved, Gopal, Gobind; deep, profound and unfathomable is he.
There is no other, none second (to him); O Nanak, he is the carefree Lord. ॥1॥
252.7: Lala: there is no one equal to him;
he alone is, himself; there will be no other.
Ever-existent, he has been for ever;
no one has found his end.
He fully pervades the worm and the elephant;
the all-pervading Being is known to be manifest in every place.
The one to whom the Lord has given his own sweet essence,
O Nanak, repeats (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, through the Guru. ॥12॥
252.8: Those who have known the relish of the spirit savour the Lord's love in Sahaj;
O Nanak, blessed, blessed, blessed are those people; their coming (into the world) is approved. ॥1॥
252.9: That one's coming (into the world) alone should be counted fruitful
whose tongue utters the praise of the Lord, Har Har.
Those who come and dwell in the Saadh's company
meditate on the Naam night and day with love.
That person, coming (into the world), stays dyed in the Naam
on whom the Creator bestows kindness and mercy.
He comes but once, and does not enter the cycle of births again;
O Nanak, he is absorbed in the sight of the Lord. ॥13॥
252.10: The One by repeating whom bliss wells up in the mind and the love of another perishes,
and pain, suffering and craving are quenched: O Nanak, merge in his Name. ॥1॥
253.1: Yaya: burn away evil-mindedness and duality;
abandoning it, you will abide in peace and Sahaj.
Yaya: go and seek the refuge of the Sants,
with whose support this world-ocean is crossed.
Yaya: that one does not come into birth (again)
who takes the Name of the One and strings it into his mind.
Yaya: with the support of the Perfect Guru, (this human) life is not lost;
O Nanak, that one has found peace in whose heart is the One. ॥14॥
253.2: The Friend of this world and the next dwells within mind and body;
the Perfect Guru has taught (this); O Nanak, one should repeat (his Name) every day. ॥1॥
253.3: Night and day remember him who will be your helper at the end.
This Maya lasts but four or six days; everyone leaves it and goes.
Whose are mother, father, son and daughter?
Home, wife, anything at all: (no one) has taken it along.
Gather such (wealth) as does not perish,
(so that) you go with honour to your own home.
Those who in Kalyug have sung (the Lord's) Kirtan in the Saadh Sangat:
O Nanak, none of them has come (into birth) again. ॥15॥
253.4: (Though they be) very handsome, of noble birth, clever, eminent, learned and wealthy,
O Nanak, those with no love for the Lord are called dead. ॥1॥
253.5: Nganga: (one may) be versed in the six Shastras,
practise drawing in, holding and letting out the breath (purak, kumbhak, rechak),
be given to knowledge and meditation, and bathe at places of pilgrimage,
cook his own food (for purity), let no one touch him, and live in the wilderness;
(but if) there is no love in his mind for the Name of the Lord, Ram,
all that he has done is perishable.
Higher than him I count the chandal
in whose mind Gopal dwells, says Nanak. ॥16॥
253.6: (People) wander the four quarters and the ten directions by the line drawn by the deeds they have done;
O Nanak, pleasure and pain, liberation and the cycle of births (come) by the writ that is written. ॥1॥
253.7: Kaka: he alone is the Creator, the maker of all causes;
no one can erase the writ he has written.
Nothing has to be done (by him) a second time;
the Maker is not one who errs.
To one he himself shows the path;
another he makes to wander in the wilderness and repent.
He himself has made his own play;
O Nanak, whatever he has given, that is what (each) has received. ॥17॥
253.8: (His servants) go on eating, spending and enjoying, (yet his) storehouses are never used up.
O Nanak, countless people repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har; there is no counting them. ॥1॥
253.9: Khakha: nothing is wanting with that almighty (Lord);
whatever he is to give, he keeps giving, whatever place (one) may go to.
The wealth of the Naam is their provision and their treasure; this is the devotees' capital.
In forgiveness, humility, bliss and Sahaj, they keep repeating (the Name of) the Treasure of virtues.
Those to whom (God) is merciful play and blossom in bliss;
they are ever rich and graceful: the riches of the Lord's Name are in their home.
No anguish, no pain, no penalty is theirs on whom he has cast his glance of grace.
O Nanak, those who are pleasing to God have come through in full. ॥18॥
254.1: Count and measure, and see within your own mind: people must surely depart.
Through the Guru, hope in passing things is erased; O Nanak, the Naam (alone) makes one whole. ॥1॥
254.2: Gaga: sing the virtues of Gobind; repeat (his Name) with every breath, every day.
What trust can be placed in the body? Do not delay, my friend.
Childhood, youth or old age: at none of these is there any bar (to death).
No one knows the hour when the noose of Jam will come and fall.
See: the learned, the meditative, the clever, (none) is to stay in this place.
That which all the world has left behind and gone, to that the fools cling.
By the Guru's grace, the one with (good) fortune on the forehead keeps remembering (the Lord).
O Nanak, those granted the wedded love of the Beloved: their coming (into the world) bears fruit. ॥19॥
254.3: All the Shastras and Vedas have been searched through; none of them tells of any other (than him).
In the beginning, from the start of the ages, now and in time to come, O Nanak, he alone is. ॥1॥
254.4: Ghagha: set this firmly in your mind: apart from the Lord there is no other.
There has been none, nor will there be; everywhere he alone is contained.
O mind, you will melt into (him) only when you come to (his) refuge.
In Kalyug the Naam is the essence, (and it is the true) act of atonement.
Many toil and toil (at other efforts), and repent;
without devotion to the Lord, where can they find steadiness?
That one has mixed and drunk the supremely sweet Amrit,
O Nanak, (that one) to whom the Guru has given the Lord's (Name). ॥20॥
254.5: (God) has sent (each one into the world) with all the days and breaths counted; they do not grow or shrink by even a sesame seed's worth.
Those who, in delusion and attachment, long to live (longer), O Nanak, are fools. ॥1॥
254.6: Nganga: death seizes those whom God has made Saakats;
they are born and die in countless forms of life, (for) they have not recognised the Lord within (Atam Ram).
Divine knowledge and meditation come only to those
on whom (God) himself, in his grace, has had them bestowed.
By counting and reckoning (deeds) no one is set free;
the pitcher of unbaked clay will surely break.
He alone (truly) lives who, while alive, has repeated (the Name);
O Nanak, (such ones) become manifest; they do not stay hidden. ॥21॥
254.7: I fix my mind on (the Lord's) lotus feet, and the inverted lotus (of the heart) blossoms.
O Nanak, through the counsel of the Sants, Gobind himself becomes manifest (in the heart). ॥1॥
254.8: Chacha: (when I) was joined to the Guru's lotus feet,
blessed, blessed was that day, and fortunate that union.
(Before,) I had wandered through the four quarters and the ten directions;
when (the Lord's) grace came, then I was granted the sight (of him).
My thoughts were made fair, and all duality perished;
in the Saadh Sangat the mind became pure.
He puts away all worry and beholds the One (everywhere),
O Nanak, the one whose eyes bear the collyrium of (the Guru's) wisdom. ॥22॥
254.9: Singing songs of Gobind's virtues, the heart grows cool and the mind is at ease.
Show such grace, O God; Nanak is the servant of your servants. ॥1॥
254.10: Chhachha: (O God,) we are your little servants,
carriers of water for the servants of your servants.
Chhachha: (grant that we) become the dust (of the feet) of your Sants;
(One who,) giving up cleverness and much cunning,
has set the support of the Sants firm in the mind:
even (that) puppet of dust has attained the supreme state,
O Nanak, the one whom the Sants help. ॥23॥
255.1: (People) swell with pride through force and oppression; (their) frail body (is given over) to vice.
Through the proud intellect they are caught in bonds; O Nanak, release (comes only) through the Name. ॥1॥
255.2: Jaja: one who thinks, I have become someone,
is held fast in that delusion, like a parrot on the nalini.
When one thinks, I am a devotee, a man of wisdom,
hereafter the Master will not count it worth a sesame seed.
When one thinks, I am a preacher (of holy discourse),
he goes about the earth like a pedlar.
The one who has slain Haumai in the Saadh Sangat,
O Nanak, meets Murari, the Lord. ॥24॥
255.3: Rise in the early hours and repeat the Naam; worship (the Lord) night and day.
No fretting will take hold of you; says Nanak, (your) troubles will end. ॥1॥
255.4: trade in the Name of Ram.
Fretting and fretting, the Saakat dies,
the one in whose heart is the love of another.
The stains and sins of your mind will fall away
(if) you hear (the Lord's) nectar-like praise in the company of the Sants.
Lust, anger and wickedness fall away (from that one),
O Nanak, on whom is the grace of the Lord of the world. ॥25॥
255.5: You may try in many ways, friend, (but) you will not be allowed to stay (here).
Says Nanak: if you worship the Lord, Har Har, with love for the Name, you will (truly) live. ॥1॥
255.6: Nyanya: know this firmly as certain, that these attachments perish.
How many have risen and gone (from here) I do not reckon, nor can I count them.
Whatever I see is passing away; with whom, then, should one keep company?
O mind, know it truly in this way: the colour of Maya is false.
That one alone knows it, that one is a Sant, who has been set apart from delusion.
(O God,) the one with whom you are well pleased you draw out of the blind well (of attachment).
The One in whose hands is all power, who is able to bring every cause about,
Nanak sings the praise of him who has brought about (this) union. ॥26॥
255.7: The bonds of birth and death are broken, and peace is found, by serving the Saadh,
O Nanak, (by one) from whose mind Gobind the King, the treasure of virtues, is never forgotten. ॥1॥
255.8: If you would serve, serve the One, from whom no one (goes away) empty.
(When he) dwells in mind, body, mouth and heart, whatever you wish comes to be.
Service in (the Lord's) mansion is given to the one on whom the Saadh is kind;
and one comes to dwell in the Saadh Sangat only when (the Lord) himself is merciful.
I have searched through many places; without the Name there is no peace.
The messengers of Jam turn away from those who merge into the company of the Saadh.
Again and again I am a sacrifice to the Sants;
O Nanak, (in their company) the sins of ages long past have been destroyed. ॥27॥
255.9: (O God,) no bar is put in the way at (your) door of those with whom you are well pleased.
Blessed, blessed indeed, O Nanak, are those whom God has made his own. ॥1॥
256.1: Thattha: they do not wound (anyone's) heart
who leave all else behind and cling to the One alone.
Those who have died clashing and jostling (with others) for the sake of Maya
Coolness came upon the one who dwelt in the company of the Sants;
there the nectar of the Name filled (that one's) soul with its taste.
The one who has become pleasing to his Master,
O Nanak, that one's mind has been cooled and calmed. ॥28॥
256.2: Countless times I bow and lie prostrate (before you), O mighty (Lord) of every power.
Keep Nanak from wavering, O God: give him your hand. ॥1॥
256.3: Dadda: this is not (your lasting) dwelling; come to know where the dwelling is.
Through the Guru's Shabad, learn the way to that dwelling.
For this dwelling one toils and labours,
yet not a jot of it goes along (at the end).
The ways of that dwelling are known to that one
on whom rests the glance (of grace) of the perfect Lord.
(Those who) have found the unmoving, true dwelling in the Saadh Sangat —
O Nanak, those people do not waver. ॥29॥
256.4: When Dharam Raj (and his messengers) began to tear down (the body), no one put up a barrier (before them).
O Nanak, those bound in kinship with the Saadh Sangat were saved by repeating (the Name of) the Lord. ॥1॥
256.5: Dhaddha: where do you go searching? The search is within this mind.
God dwells with you; why do you roam from forest to forest?
In the Saadh Sangat, pull down the mound of the dreadful proud intellect;
(then) you will find peace, dwell in Sahaj, and be filled with joy beholding (the Lord).
(While) the mound (of ego) stands, one is born only to die, and suffers the pains of the womb and of births;
drunk with attachment, one stays clinging (to Maya), and, crying I, I, keeps coming and going.
Crumbling, crumbling, (we) have now fallen at the refuge of the holy;
the nooses of pain have been cut, and, O Nanak, (the Lord) has merged (us into himself). ॥30॥
256.6: (Dharam Raj says:) Where the Saadhs worship Gobind and sing his Kirtan day by day, O Nanak,
(go there, and) neither I nor you will escape: do not go near it, my messengers. ॥1॥
256.7: Nanna: on the battlefield (of life), the one who conquers the self wins.
One who fights Haumai and duality and dies (to the self) becomes a glorious warrior.
One who, by the teaching of the perfect Guru, wipes out the ego and dies while yet alive,
conquers the mind and meets the Lord: his is the garb of the warrior.
He counts no one as his own; the One alone is his shelter and stay.
Night and day he keeps remembering God, the boundless Being.
He makes this mind the dust (of the feet) of all; such are the deeds he lives by.
He understands (the Lord's) Hukam and (knows) lasting peace; O Nanak, he receives what was written (for him). ॥31॥
256.8: I would offer body, mind and wealth to the one who would unite me with God.
O Nanak, (meeting him,) doubt and fear are cut away, and the watching eye of Jam is gone. ॥1॥
256.9: Tata: love him, Gobind the King, the treasure of virtues;
you will obtain the fruits your mind longs for, and your burning will leave you.
Dread of the road of Jam is gone for the one in whose mind the Name dwells.
You will reach the high state, your understanding will be lit, and you will find a place in (the Lord's) mansion.
Wealth does not go along with (anyone at the end), nor house, nor youth, nor power.
In the company of the Sants keep remembering (the Lord); this alone will serve you.
No burning grief remains at all when (the Lord) himself takes the fever away.
O Nanak, (the Lord) cherishes us; he himself is mother and father. ॥32॥
257.1: (They) have grown weary toiling in many ways, yet are not satisfied, and (their) craving has not left them.
Amassing and amassing (Maya), the Saakats have died; O Nanak, Maya did not go with them. ॥1॥
257.2: Thatha: no one stays (here) for ever; why, then, do you stretch out your feet (as if to stay)?
You practise countless frauds, tricks and deceits, striving for Maya alone.
You fill your purse, you toil, and you drop exhausted, you fool;
(yet) it is of no use to the soul at the last hour.
You will find steadiness if you worship Gobind and take the teaching of the Sants;
love the One for ever: this is the true love.
(The Lord is) the cause, the doer and the one who has all things done; every means is in the hands of the One alone.
Says Nanak: wherever you set them, (O Lord,) there they are set; the creatures are helpless. ॥33॥
257.3: (The Lord's) servants have seen the One as the giver of everything;
with every breath they keep remembering (him); O Nanak, beholding (him) is what sustains them. ॥1॥
257.4: Dada: the Giver is the One, who gives to all;
his giving never runs short; numberless are (his) brimming storehouses.
O foolish mind, why have you forgotten him?
My friend, the fault lies with no one;
God (himself) has made the bond of attachment to Maya.
Those whose pain you yourself take away, (O Lord,)
O Nanak, each of them is fulfilled, through the Guru. ॥34॥
257.5: O my soul, take the One as your sole support, and put away hope in others;
O Nanak, the Naam should be meditated on; (then) every task turns out well. ॥1॥
257.6: Dhadha: the wandering (of the mind) ends only when one's dwelling is in the company of the Sants.
(O Lord,) when you yourself show grace from the very source, then light dawns in the mind.
They whose wealth is lasting are the true merchants,
whose capital is the Lord, Har Har, and who have traded in the Name.
Steadfastness, praise and honour become the lot of the one
who has heard the Name of the Lord, Har Har, with (his) ears.
The one in whose heart (the Lord) stays absorbed, through the Guru:
O Nanak, that servant (of the Lord) has received greatness. ॥35॥
257.7: O Nanak, (those who) have repeated the Naam, the Naam alone, with love, within and without,
have been taught by the Perfect Guru; in the Saadh Sangat there is no hell (for them). ॥1॥
257.8: Nana: they do not fall into hell
in whose mind and body the Naam dwells.
Those who, through the Guru, repeat the Naam, the treasure,
do not waste away in the poison of Maya.
those to whom the Guru has given the mantra of the Naam.
They are full of the Lord's Amrit, the treasure of treasures;
there (within them), O Nanak, the unstruck instruments play. ॥36॥
258.1: The Guru, the Supreme Lord, has kept the honour (of the one) who has given up deceit, attachment and vice;
O Nanak, let us worship that One alone, who has no end and no shore on either side. ॥1॥
258.2: Pappa: (the Lord) is beyond measure; (no one) has found his limit.
The Lord King is beyond reach, the purifier of the fallen.
who meet the Saadh and repeat the Naam, the Amrit.
Deceit, treachery and attachment are erased through (your) praise
in the one whom you yourself protect, O Master of the world.
He alone is the Emperor, with the canopy over (his) head;
O Nanak, there is no other, no second (like him). ॥37॥
258.3: The nooses are cut, the wanderings are over; victory has come by conquering the mind.
O Nanak, steadiness was found from the Guru, and the rounds (of birth) are over for ever. ॥1॥
258.4: Phapha: wandering and wandering (through births), you have come;
(now) in Kalyug you have obtained the (human) body, so rarely given.
Such a chance will not come to hand again.
Repeat the Naam, and the nooses (of Maya) will be cut;
there will be no coming and going again and again.
Repeat the remembrance of that One, the One alone.
Be merciful, O God, the Creator,
and unite helpless Nanak with yourself. ॥38॥
258.5: Hear (my) prayer, O Supreme Lord, Gopal, merciful to the meek:
for Nanak, the dust of the Saadhs' feet is comfort, wealth, many pleasures and delights. ॥1॥
258.6: Babba: those who know Brahm (God) are the (true) Brahmins;
(true) Vaishnavs are they who, through the Guru, (keep) the dharma of purity.
The hero is one who wipes out the evil in himself;
(Man) is bound by his own bond of I, I (Haumai),
(yet) the blind one puts the blame on others.
All talk and cleverness come to nothing;
only the one to whom you, (O Lord,) give understanding knows (this), says Nanak. ॥39॥
258.7: In your mind worship the Lord, the breaker of fear, the destroyer of sin and sorrow.
Those in whose heart (the Lord) has come to dwell through the company of the Sants, O Nanak, do not wander in delusion. ॥1॥
258.8: this whole world is a dream.
Heavenly beings, men, goddesses and gods have wandered in delusion;
Siddhas, seekers and (the likes of) Brahma have wandered in delusion.
Wandering on and on in delusion, people have been led astray.
This Maya is hard to cross, and most perilous.
Those who, through the Guru, have wiped out delusion, fear and attachment,
O Nanak, have found the supreme peace. ॥40॥
258.9: Maya wavers in many ways, (yet) the mind clings to it;
(O Lord,) the one you keep from begging (for Maya) is in love with the Name alone, says Nanak. ॥1॥
258.10: Mamma: the one who begs is ignorant;
the all-knowing Giver goes on giving.
What he gave, he gave once (for all).
O foolish mind, why do you keep crying out?
Whenever you ask, you ask for things other (than the Name),
through which no one has ever fared well.
If you must ask, then ask for the One alone,
by whom, says Nanak, you will cross to the far shore. ॥41॥
259.1: Their understanding is complete, and they are foremost, whose minds hold the teaching of the Perfect Guru;
those who have come to know their God, O Nanak, are blessed with good fortune. ॥1॥
259.2: Mamma: one who has recognised (the Lord's) secret
is content (in mind) as soon as he meets the Saadh Sangat.
Pain and pleasure are weighed alike in his mind;
he is spared from being born into hell or heaven.
(He sees that) the same (Lord) is with (all), and the same (Lord) is untouched (by all);
the Being fills each and every heart, (and he) sees (this) distinctly.
In that relish (of the Lord) he alone has found peace;
O Nanak, Maya does not stain him. ॥42॥
259.3: Listen, friends, companions, dear ones: without the Lord there is no release.
O Nanak, their bonds are cut who fall at the Guru's feet. ॥1॥
259.4: Yaya: (people) make efforts of many kinds,
(but) how far can success go without the one Name?
The effort by which release comes
is the company of the Saadh.
Everyone holds (in mind) this longing to be saved,
(but) without meditating on him there is no saving.
He alone is the boat that carries across, mighty to save;
save (us), the virtueless, O Lord of men.
Those to whom (the Lord) himself has given this understanding in mind, word and deed,
O Nanak, their understanding has come to light. ॥43॥
259.5: Hold no grudge against anyone; reflect on your own self.
Live humbly in the world; O Nanak, by (the Lord's) gracious glance you will cross over. ॥1॥
259.6: Rara: (become the dust of the Lord,) whose dust all (creation) becomes;
give up pride, and the arrears (in the account of your deeds) will be cleared.
O brother, you will win through on the battlefield (of the world) and in the Lord's court
when, through the Guru, you are lovingly attuned to the Name of Ram.
Little by little the vices fall away,
countless as they are, through the Shabad of the Perfect Guru.
Dyed in love, they are intoxicated with the relish of the Name,
those on whom, O Nanak, the Lord, the Guru, has bestowed this gift. ॥44॥
259.7: Greed, falsehood, vice and disease dwell in this body;
one who has drunk the Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, through the Guru, O Nanak, dwells in peace. ॥1॥
259.8: Lala: anyone to whom I apply the medicine (of the Name),
his pains and sorrows vanish in an instant.
One who holds the medicine of the Name dear in the heart
is not touched by disease even in a dream.
The Lord's medicine is in all hearts, O brother,
(but) without the Perfect Guru, the way (to take it) is not found.
The Perfect Guru has set the regimen (to keep with it);
then, O Nanak, pain does not come again. ॥45॥
259.9: Vasudev (the Lord) fills every place; in no place is he wanting.
He is with (all), within and without; O Nanak, how can anything be hidden (from him)? ॥1॥
259.10: Vava: bear enmity toward no one;
Brahm (God) dwells within each and every heart.
(but) only a rare one, by the Guru's grace, has reached (him).
Enmity and opposition are gone from the minds of those
who, through the Guru, listen to the Lord's Kirtan.
Above all castes and marks stands the one
who, O Nanak, utters Har Har through the Guru. ॥46॥
260.1: Crying I, I, the foolish, ignorant Saakats have passed (their lives);
writhing, they died like the thirsty; O Nanak, (it was) by the deeds they had earned. ॥1॥
260.2: Rarra: the rankling strife (of the mind) ends in the company of the Saadh;
worship of the Name is the essence of (all) rites and religious duties.
The one in whose heart the Beautiful (Lord) has come to dwell:
his strife is ended and destroyed.
The foolish Saakats keep up strife,
in whose hearts are the vices of the proud intellect.
Rarra: the one who through the Guru has wiped out the strife
is given understanding in an instant, O Nanak. ॥47॥
260.3: O mind, take hold of the Saadh's support; give up argument and cleverness.
O Nanak, the one in whose mind the Guru's teaching dwells has good fortune (written) on the forehead. ॥1॥
260.4: Sassa: (O God,) defeated, we have now fallen at (your) refuge.
The Shastras, the Smritis and the Vedas cry it aloud,
and searching and searching, (we too) have searched and reflected:
without worship of the Lord there is no release.
With every breath we go astray;
you are all-powerful, beyond count, boundless.
O Merciful One, keep (the honour) of the one who has fallen at your refuge.
Says Nanak, we are your children, O Gopal. ॥48॥
260.5: When self-conceit was gone, then peace came, and mind and body were made whole.
O Nanak, (then) the One worthy of praise came into sight. ॥1॥
260.6: Khakha: I praise him with all my heart,
who in an instant fills the empty to the brim.
When the mortal becomes truly humble,
(he) meditates night and day on God, who is free of all desire.
If it pleases the Master, he gives that one peace.
Such is the Supreme Lord, beyond all count:
(he) forgives countless sins in an instant.
O Nanak, the Master is merciful for ever. ॥49॥
260.7: I tell you the truth, listen, O my mind: fall at the refuge of the Lord King.
O Nanak, when (one) gives up all argument and cleverness, (the Lord) takes (that one) into himself. ॥1॥
260.8: Sassa: give up cleverness, you ignorant one;
God is not won over by cunning or by commanding.
You may practise cleverness in a thousand ways,
(yet) not one of them goes with you.
Repeat him, him alone, day and night;
O soul, (he alone) goes with you as your companion.
The one whom (God) himself sets to serve the Saadh,
O Nanak, no suffering touches him. ॥50॥
260.9: Speak Har, Har with the mouth; (when the Lord) dwells in the mind, peace comes.
O Nanak, he pervades all; he is in every place and in the spaces between. ॥1॥
260.10: I look, and see the Lord filling every heart of all.
Ever and for ever (the Lord) has been the destroyer of suffering: (this is) the Guru's wisdom.
When Haumai is shed, bliss comes to that one; where there is no Haumai, there (God) himself is.
Through the power of the company of the Sants, the sufferings of birth and death are destroyed.
The one who lovingly holds firm (in the heart) the Name of the Merciful (Lord),
in the company of the Sants, (God) becomes kind (to him).
No one has done anything apart from him;
O Nanak, all has come from God. ॥51॥
261.1: If (our deeds) are reckoned, there is no release anywhere; moment by moment we go astray.
O Forgiver, forgive (us), and carry Nanak across. ॥1॥
261.2: (The mortal) is untrue to his salt, a sinner, a stranger (to God), of little understanding;
he does not know the One, the very essence, who gave him soul, body and comforts.
For the gain of Maya he goes searching in the ten directions,
(but) not for an instant does he keep in mind God, the bountiful Giver.
Greed, falsehood, vice and attachment: this is the wealth (he holds) in his mind.
With lechers, thieves and great slanderers his (life) goes by.
(O God,) if it pleases you, you forgive the false together with the true.
O Nanak, if it pleases the Supreme Lord, stones float on water. ॥52॥
261.3: Eating, drinking, playing and laughing, (we) have wandered through many births.
Lift (us) out of the world-ocean, God; Nanak leans on you (alone). ॥1॥
261.4: Playing and playing, (the soul) has come through many births, suffering pain.
Meeting the Saadh, merging in the True Guru's word, (its) troubles are ended.
(It) took up forgiveness, gathered truth, and ate the Amrit of the Naam;
the Master's great grace came, (and it found) bliss, peace and rest.
(It) carried its trading through, made great profit, and came home with honour;
the Guru gave (it) true comfort, and the Lord came and met (it).
(The Lord) himself has done (all), and he himself does it; he himself is ahead and behind.
O Nanak, let us praise him alone, who pervades every heart. ॥53॥
261.5: O God, treasure of mercy, merciful One, (we) have come to (your) refuge.
O Nanak, (when) the One, the imperishable Lord, dwells in the mind, (one) is filled with joy. ॥1॥
261.6: God has set the three worlds within letters;
with letters, written again and again, the Vedas were pondered.
In letters are the Shastras, the Smritis and the Puranas;
in letters, sacred sound, speech and exposition.
In letters (are told) fear and doubt and the way of release (from them);
in letters, rites, deeds, purity and dharma.
All that is seen is within letters;
(but) O Nanak, the Supreme Lord is untouched (by them). ॥54॥
261.7: The pen is in the hand of the Inaccessible; (he) writes (the destiny) on (every) forehead.
He of incomparable beauty is entwined with all.
(O God,) your praise cannot be told by the mouth.
Beholding your sight, Nanak is enraptured, and is a sacrifice (to you). ॥1॥
261.8: O Unshakeable One, O Supreme Lord, Imperishable, Destroyer of sins,
O Perfect One, O All-pervading, Destroyer of suffering, Treasure of virtues,
O Companion, O Formless, O Nirgun, Support of all,
O Gobind, O Treasury of virtues, in whom discernment ever abides,
O Lord beyond the beyond, Har Hare: you are, and you will be.
O ever-present with the Sants, Support of those who have none:
O Master, I am your lowly servant; I am without virtue, I have no virtue at all.
Grant Nanak the gift of the Naam, that I may keep it strung in my heart. ॥55॥
262.1: The Gurdev is mother, the Gurdev is father, the Gurdev is the Master, the Supreme God.
The Gurdev is the friend who destroys ignorance; the Gurdev is kinsman and brother born of the same womb.
The Gurdev is the Giver who teaches the Lord's Name; the Gurdev's mantra is one whose power nothing can stop.
The Gurdev is the embodiment of peace, truth and wisdom; the Gurdev is a paaras whose touch surpasses even the paaras.
The Gurdev is the tirath, the pool of Amrit; to bathe in the Guru's wisdom is beyond all else.
The Gurdev is the Creator, the remover of all sins; the Gurdev makes the fallen pure.
The Gurdev is from the beginning, from the start of the ages, in every age; repeating the Gurdev's mantra, the Lord's Name, one is saved.
O God, in your grace join (us) to the Gurdev's company, holding fast to which we foolish sinners may swim across.
The Gurdev is the True Guru, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God; O Nanak, salutation to the Gurdev, the Lord.
This salok is to be read at the beginning and at the end (of the Bavan Akhri).
